text_blocks.snippet: Treatment for high blood pressure (hypertension) involves a mix of healthy lifestyle habits and prescription medicines outlined by the Mayo Clinic.
snippet_highlighted_words: a mix of healthy lifestyle habits and prescription medicines

list.snippet: DASH diet: Eat more fruits, vegetables, and low-fat dairy. Cut daily salt intake to under 2,000 milligrams.
Exercise: Do regular aerobic workouts, such as brisk walking, for about 30 minutes most days.
Weight loss: Shed extra pounds to lower the workload on your heart and blood vessels.
Limit alcohol: Reduce alcohol consumption to help lower your blood pressure readings.

text_blocks.snippet: Doctors often prescribe one or more of these main drug classes:

list.snippet: ACE inhibitors and ARBs: Relax and widen your blood vessels by blocking specific natural chemicals. Examples include lisinopril and losartan.
Calcium channel blockers: Keep calcium out of muscle cells in your heart and arteries to let blood vessels relax. An example is amlodipine.
Thiazide diuretics: Water pills that help your kidneys flush out extra salt and water. An example is hydrochlorothiazide.
Any other health conditions you have (such as diabetes or kidney disease)
